evidence_test: cd referee && python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_llm_call.py'  # Prompt.*, Process.*, NotSent.*, Outcomes.*, CommandLine.*. 29d:43 names group prompt (MF15, 'tipli girdi -> prompt sha256; tip disi alan girmez') but no page gives its command, stdin, output fields or cases (29h-29j stop at MF13), and tohum/26 gives no payload for a cost row of part cost. My choices, each bound by a test, to be replaced when the seed writes the interface (as seed-018, seed-020 were): (a) command: python -m dispatcher.llm_call prompt, stdin {template, input} -> {prompt_sha256, system_sha256}; exit 0, 2 unusable (both null). (b) template exactly {name, system, body, input, output}; a type is {field: kind}, kinds string, integer (not true, within +-(2^53-1)), boolean, strings; one checker for input and structured output. (c) 'tip disi alan girmez' read as refused, not dropped: a vector's changed input with an extra field must not give the expected sha256, and dropping it would give the same sha, so the vector could not tell the two. A missing field and every wrong kind are refused too. (d) body placeholders {field}, {{ and }} literal, any other brace refused, every placeholder declared and every field used; each value enters as its RFC 8785 form (strings quoted and escaped), so a value cannot add template text; prompt_sha256 = sha256(UTF-8 prompt), system_sha256 = sha256(system). (e) the CLI's shape I assume (no seed page gives it; the real one is asama-0/10a #model): --output-format json prints one object {type: result, subtype, is_error, result, stop_reason, total_cost_usd, modelUsage, structured_output}; the served models are modelUsage's keys and must be exactly [model]; a 429 is the text 'API Error: 429' in result. A network error without a status is cli_error (unresolved), not outage: tohum/24 counts network errors as outages, but I found no stable form to recognise them by. (f) flags: -p --output-format json --tools '' --setting-sources '' --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands --no-session-persistence --model --max-budget-usd --system-prompt --json-schema (names checked against claude --help of CLI 2.1.293, the version in this session); prompt on stdin; env exactly PATH, HOME, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (fresh), CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN; cwd a fresh empty directory; the pin is the CLI file's sha512 (requirements/claude-cli is in the seed, not here). (g) the stage brake: no call when spent + cap > budget, spent summed from part cost, kind cost rows with the same payload.budget, the verified ledger plus this cycle's recorded rows; a cost row the brake cannot read stops the call. (h) the cost row: part cost, kind cost, derivation tool, trust observed, payload {tool, template, budget, model_requested, models_served, outcome, reason, cost_usd_micros (CLI estimate rounded up; the cap on a timeout or an unreadable result), cost_source, cap_usd_micros, prompt_sha256, system_sha256, duration_ms}; recorded for every started process, written by the cycle's one ledger.append commit (calls 10 -> 15). (i) found while writing it: a payload field named budget_key holding the policy key name is refused by ledger.append, because MF2's scan reads any *_key field with 8+ characters as an assigned secret; the field is named budget. Any later row schema with a *_key field (tohum/26's names include none today) would meet the same rule.
